title: aw says /aw/
parentNote: Today is aw, the wide-open sound in saw and claw. The two letters make one sound and the w does not speak on its own, which is the same deal your child already struck with ay in day and ow in snow — say that out loud, because noticing the pattern is worth more than learning this one team. The slip to expect is the a going back to its old job, so claw comes out as clah-w or even cla. If that happens, cover the w with your finger, let them say the a, then uncover it and say the whole thing yourself: aw. One more thing worth knowing is where this team lives. aw sits at the end of a word (saw, jaw, draw) or just before one last sound (hawk, lawn, crawl), and almost never at the front, so it is a team to hunt for in the back half of the word.

activities.mouthCue: Drop your jaw and let your lips go round, and hold it: aaaw. It is the shape your mouth makes at the doctor.
activities.prompt: A new team. Two letters, one sound, and the w does not get a turn of its own.

Two sounds in the whole word. Hold the new one at the end.
Now the team is in the middle, with one sound after it.
The long one. Two teams in it. Sound out see, then sound out saw, then push them together.
All three start with an s. The end of the word is where the work is.
Listen right to the last sound, and then to the one in the middle.
This one is hard. All three start with dr. Two of them have a team that says aw and one does not.

activities.text: A big hawk did sit up in the oak, and I saw it drop fast.
Meg said, "Do you want to draw a fox?" and she did hand me a pen.
The cat did yawn and then did stick out its claws.
"Do not sit on the wet straw!" said Dad, and we did jump up off it.

activities.title: The hawk on the lawn
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: At sun up I did peep out, and I saw a big bird sat on the lawn.
It did not hop and it did not peck. It did not want to go.
Dad said, "That is a hawk. Do not run at it," and we did stand still.
The hawk did lift up a claw, and it did not set it back.
Meg said, "It is stuck!" and she did point at the grass.
A long straw did get stuck on that claw, and the hawk did tug and tug.
"Get me the ham," said Dad, and I did run in and get it.
He did set the ham on the lawn and did creep up next to the hawk.
The hawk did peck at the ham, and Dad did slip the straw off its claw.
Up it did go, off the lawn and up past the big oak.
Meg said, "Do you want to draw it?" and so we did sit on the step and draw a hawk.
